blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Reading a cash flow statement means looking for alignment between profit and cash. In a healthy business, the two move together, roughly. When they drift apart — profit high, cash weak — the cash flow statement tells you where the gap went. Usually it is working capital: receivables growing, inventory building, payables being paid down.

The three sections each tell a different part of the story. Operating cash shows whether the business generates its own money. Investing cash shows where that money is being put to work. Financing cash shows what is being borrowed or repaid.

A company whose operating cash is consistently strong has a quiet, durable kind of health that no profit-and-loss statement alone can prove. Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact.

items.q: According to the text, what should you look for when reading a cash flow statement?
items.why: "Reading a cash flow statement means looking for alignment between profit and cash."

items.q: When profit is high but cash is weak, where does the gap usually go?
items.why: "Usually it is working capital: receivables growing, inventory building, payables being paid down."

items.q: Which section shows whether the business generates its own money?
items.why: "Operating cash shows whether the business generates its own money."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A healthy profit-and-loss statement is enough to prove a company is healthy.
Strong operating cash is a good sign of durable health.
The three sections tell different parts of the same story.
A profitable company can still be running short of cash.
items.why: Inferência: "a durable kind of health that no P&L alone can prove" — o texto argumenta justamente que o lucro sozinho não prova a saúde.

items.q: What does "Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact" suggest?
options: Cash and profit mean the same thing
Cash is harder to measure than profit
Profit depends on accounting judgement, while cash is verifiable
items.why: Inferência: o lucro envolve estimativas contábeis; o caixa é o dinheiro que de fato entrou ou saiu.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando uma nova analista sobre um demonstrativo de fluxo de caixa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Alright, look at this one with me. On paper it is a good year — profit is up almost twenty per cent. But watch what happens when we go to the cash flow statement.

Operating cash is barely positive. Almost all the profit has disappeared somewhere, and the somewhere is right here: working capital. Receivables have jumped, because sales grew fast and nobody chased the money in. Inventory has built up as well. So the company earned the profit, but it has not collected it yet — it is sitting in customers' hands and on warehouse shelves.

Now, this is not a crisis on its own. A growing business often consumes cash for a while. What worries me is the trend. Working capital has grown faster than sales for three quarters running. That is the pattern you want to catch early, before financing cash has to fill the hole with new borrowing.

So when you read one of these, do not stop at the profit line. Follow the money into operating cash, and ask one question: is this business actually generating the cash it claims to earn?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is unusual about the year Sophie is describing?
options: The company reported no profit at all
Profit is up, yet operating cash is barely positive
items.why: "profit is up almost twenty per cent" mas "Operating cash is barely positive."

items.q: Where has most of the profit gone?
options: Into working capital — receivables and inventory
items.why: "the somewhere is right here: working capital. Receivables have jumped… Inventory has built up as well."

items.q: Why does Sophie say the profit has not really been collected?
options: Because it is sitting in receivables and unsold inventory
Because it was used to repay loans
Because it was reinvested in new projects
items.why: "it is sitting in customers' hands and on warehouse shelves" — ainda não virou caixa.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "before financing cash has to fill the hole"?
options: The company may soon need to borrow to cover the missing cash
The inventory will be written off
The profit will have to be restated
items.why: Inferência: se o caixa operacional não cobre a operação, sobra recorrer a novos empréstimos (caixa de financiamento).

items.q: What is Sophie really teaching the analyst to do?
options: Trust the profit line above everything else
Look past the profit and check whether the cash is actually there
Avoid reading cash flow statements when profit is high
items.why: Inferência: "do not stop at the profit line. Follow the money into operating cash."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "In a healthy business, profit and cash stay in alignment." Here, alignment means…
items.why: Alignment = alinhamento: lucro e caixa andando juntos.

items.q: "When profit and cash drift apart, something is absorbing the money." To drift apart means to…
options: gradually move away from each other
items.why: To drift apart = distanciar-se, afastar-se aos poucos.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Operating cash shows whether the business can ___ its own money."
items.why: To generate = gerar; o caixa operacional mostra se a empresa produz o próprio dinheiro.

items.q: "Strong operating cash gives a company a durable kind of health." Durable means…
items.why: Durable = durável, que se sustenta ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The gap between reported profit and actual cash showed up as ___."
items.why: Gap = lacuna; na lição, a diferença entre lucro e caixa aparece no capital de giro (recebíveis e estoque).

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem ao analisar demonstrativos financeiros. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We need to free up cash tied in receivables." To free up cash means to…
items.why: Free up cash = liberar caixa que estava preso (por exemplo, em recebíveis ou estoque).

items.q: "Inventory keeps building up in the warehouse." To build up means to…
items.why: Build up = acumular-se aos poucos.

items.q: "The company had to take on new debt to cover the gap." To take on debt means to…
items.why: Take on = assumir, contrair (uma dívida, uma responsabilidade).

items.q: "Nobody chased up the overdue invoices." To chase up means to…
options: follow up to get them paid
items.why: Chase up = cobrar, correr atrás de algo pendente (aqui, faturas em atraso).

items.q: "Once collections improve, the cash will come in." To come in here means the cash will…
items.why: Come in = entrar, chegar (o dinheiro efetivamente entrando no caixa).
